title: Relative flatness is equivalent across elementary module devissage
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, $s=f(x)$. Let $g:(X',x')\to(X,x)$ and $e:(S',s')\to(S,s)$ be elementary etale neighbourhoods (etale and inducing isomorphisms of residue fields at the marked points), and let $f':X'\to S'$ satisfy $fg=ef'$. Suppose $X',Z',Y',S'$ are affine, $i:Z'\to X'$ is a closed immersion of finite presentation, $\pi:Z'\to Y'$ is finite over $S'$, $h:Y'\to S'$ is smooth of relative dimension $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$ with geometrically integral fibres, and $\mathcal G$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{Z'}$-module with $i_*\mathcal G\cong g^*\mathcal F$. Let $z'\in Z'$ satisfy $i(z')=x'$, put $y'=\pi(z')$, and assume $h(y')=s'$, $\pi^{-1}(y')=\{z'\}$ and $\kappa(y')/\kappa(s')$ purely transcendental. These are precisely the elementary devissage data of [lem-trf-elementary-module-devissage], with module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]; explicitly $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $\mathcal F_s$ is the pullback of $\mathcal F$ to $X_s$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Schemes, affine spectra, quasi-coherence, finite type, dimension, smoothness, etaleness, finite morphisms, closed immersions, finite presentation of morphisms, residue fields, integrality and purely transcendental extensions have the meanings of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-trf-purely-transcendental-extension]. The following conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ on some neighbourhood of $x$; $\mathcal G$ is flat over $S'$ on some neighbourhood of $z'$; $\pi_*\mathcal G$ is flat over $S'$ on some neighbourhood of $y'$. Also the following stalkwise conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$; $\mathcal G_{z'}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$; $(\pi_*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$. Flatness over a base means flatness of these module stalks, as in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. No local finite-presentation assumption on $f$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 057U, lemma-devissage-flat, both neighbourhood and stalkwise assertions.

proof.text: Put $H=g^*\mathcal F\cong i_*\mathcal G$. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Apply [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness] to $e:S'\to S$ and the $\mathcal O_{S',f'(u)}$-module $H_u$, for every $u\in X'$. This says exactly that $H_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,ef'(u)}$ if and only if it is flat over $\mathcal O_{S',f'(u)}$. Therefore the stalk criterion in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] equates flatness of $H$ over $S$ and over $S'$ on any fixed open of $X'$. This base comparison is the etale local-ring result, not a consequence of faithful flatness alone.

source.place: Tag 057U, use of Tags 05B9 and 05BA; preliminary base comparison.

proof.text: Let (4) mean that $H$ is flat over $S$ on a neighbourhood of $x'$. Since $g$ is etale, it is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For each $u\in X'$, [lem-trf-relative-flatness-source-cover] gives that $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at $g(u)$ exactly when $H$ is flat over $S$ at $u$; thus this also proves the marked-stalk comparison over the original base. If (1) holds on $W\ni x$, its inverse image is a neighbourhood of $x'$ and the pointwise equivalence gives (4). Conversely, if (4) holds on $W'\ni x'$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] says $g(W')$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$. Every point there has a preimage in $W'$, so the same equivalence gives (1) on $g(W')$. Step 1 allows (4) to be expressed using $S'$ instead.

source.place: Tag 057U, (1) iff (4), using Morphisms Tags 02JZ and 02GW.

proof.text: For every $z\in Z'$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] identifies $H_{i(z)}$ with $\mathcal G_z$, linearly over $\mathcal O_{X',i(z)}$; restricting scalars makes this an $\mathcal O_{S',h\pi(z)}$-linear isomorphism because $i$ is over $S'$. Outside $i(Z')$ the stalk of $H$ is zero by the same node, hence flat: tensoring with zero sends every injection to the injection $0\to0$. Thus relative flatness of $H$ on an open $V$ is equivalent to that of $\mathcal G$ on $i^{-1}V$, using [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Given an open $U\subseteq Z'$ containing $z'$, the closed embedding in [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives an open $V\subseteq X'$ with $i^{-1}V=U$ and $x'\in V$ (write $U=Z'\cap V$ in the subspace topology). This proves (4) iff (2), and also identifies the two marked stalks over $S'$.

source.place: Tag 057U, closed-immersion neighbourhood and stalk comparison; topology written out.

proof.text: For use in the affine comparison, specialize [lem-pc-affine-cover-module-tensor-flat-criterion] with $T=A$, $q=1_A$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and, for an affine $W$, the one-member affine cover $U_0=W$. The identity base-change pullback is the original module by the pullback universal property [def-pc-module-pullback]; multiplication identifies $A\otimes_A A$ with $A$ and $A\otimes_A N$ with $N$ (inverse $n\mapsto1\otimes n$). Consequently, for a quasi-coherent module $M$ on an affine scheme $W$ over $S'=\operatorname{Spec}A$, flatness over $S'$ is equivalent to $A$-flatness of $\Gamma(W,M)$. This is a direct specialization of the cited affine-cover criterion, with no finiteness or Noetherian assumption.

Since $\pi$ is finite, it is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so inverse images of affine opens are affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Also $\pi_*\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change]. Suppose (2) holds on $U
i z'$. By [lem-trf-finite-singleton-fibre-localization] choose $V
i y'$ with $\pi^{-1}V\subseteq U$, then shrink $V$ to an affine neighbourhood. Thus $\mathcal G$ is flat over $S'$ on the affine $\pi^{-1}V$. By Step 4 its sections are flat over $A=\Gamma(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$. By the definition of pushforward, these are precisely $\Gamma(V,\pi_*\mathcal G)$ with the same $A$-action. Step 4 gives (3) on $V$. Conversely, given (3), choose an affine $V
i y'$ inside that flat neighbourhood. The same section equality and Step 4 imply that $\mathcal G$ is flat on $\pi^{-1}V
i z'$, proving (2).

source.place: Tag 057U, (2) iff (3), with Tag 05B8(1) and the omitted affine-neighbourhood details.

proof.text: For the marked stalks, [lem-trf-relative-flatness-source-cover] applied to $g$ at $x'$ gives $\mathcal F_x$ flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ iff $H_{x'}$ is flat over that same ring; flatness of $g$ follows from [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness] to the $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$-module $H_{x'}$ to replace its base by $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks], $H_{x'}\cong\mathcal G_{z'}$ is linear after restriction to this base ring, as checked in Step 3. Finally, [lem-trf-finite-singleton-fibre-localization] gives $(\pi_*\mathcal G)_{y'}\cong\mathcal G_{z'}$ linearly over $\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$ and hence over $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$ since $h(y')=s'$. Flatness is invariant under these module isomorphisms, so (a), (b), and (c) are equivalent. This uses the cited canonical stalk comparison; it makes no unsupported identification of two localized algebras.
